request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user a "Watched total": the due-totals of everyone they watch, added up, or 0.00 when they watch no one. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

It's a front-end-only change. Each person row already says whether the current user watches that person, and the screen already works out each person's due-total, so no server or database change was needed.

- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` adds up the due-totals of the watched people, using the same per-person figures as the existing "My crew total". So it respects the sheet's cap and holds, and people with no due figure count as nothing.
- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/header/header.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` input, shown as `watched-due-total` next to the other figures, in the same number format as the rest of the header.

The total updates on screen straight away when someone is watched or unwatched.
